author: reek
body: Literal patterns must be tested, whether they stand alone or sit inside a constructor pattern.

author: reek
body: Two silent miscompiles are pinned here, both found 2026-07-20 and both of the worst kind: they compiled clean, raised no diagnostic, and returned a confident wrong answer.

author: reek
body: The first: a literal nested in a constructor pattern was never compared. `bind-ctor-fields` bound variable sub-patterns and dropped everything else, and `EmitPatternResult` carried one patch slot so a second test had nowhere to be reported. Every arm whose CONSTRUCTOR matched won, so `is BInt (0)` matched any BInt, and a four-way operator dispatch collapsed onto whichever arm came first. In the tree this was apps/cvmm/Calculator treating every operator as plus and apps/browser/PageCompiler taking the then-branch of every conditional.

author: reek
body: The second: a Text literal pattern compared a pointer against `pat-lit-to-integer` of its own spelling, so `is "sin" ->` matched nothing at any nesting depth.

author: reek
body: Every case below must therefore reach a DIFFERENT arm. A test where the arms return the same value could not tell either bug from a working compiler.

author: reek
body: A literal beside a binder, and two literals in one pattern. The binder must still bind while the literal is tested.

author: reek
body: The same two questions without a constructor around them. Integer literals here always worked; Text literals never did.
